title: A comparison of scale psychometrics and cultural mistrust critical items on the MMPI-3 across Black and White male prison inmates.
titleZh: MMPI-3在黑人与白人男性监狱囚犯中的量表心理测量学及文化不信任关键条目比较
abstract: Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory-3 (MMPI-3) scale scores and cultural mistrust critical items are examined for race bias. The present study compared scale psychometrics and responses to previously identified cultural mistrust critical items on the MMPI-3 across Black (= 141) and White (= 242) male prison inmates. We first examined the generalizability of Anestis et al.'s (2023) comparison of MMPI-3 scales across Black and White college students using a sample with higher rates of externalizing psychopathology. We compared the validity of MMPI-3 scale scores in predicting scores on the Antisocial Behavior Questionnaire (Sellbom & Verona, 2007; Sellbom et al., 2012) and the Inventory of Depression and Anxiety Symptoms-Second Version (Watson et al., 2012) across race. We found evidence of small effect size slope and intercept bias in predicting some conceptually relevant criteria, with our overall findings converging with those of Anestis et al. (2023), indicating that the MMPI-3 scales generally performed comparably across Black and White prison inmates. We also sought to expand on previous findings related to a set of cultural mistrust critical items, finding significant differential endorsement between Black and White inmates on five of the nine items identified by Dixon et al. (2023). Implications and recommendations for future research are discussed. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).
